articles.title: Data Center Construction Restrictions Approved by Voters Across Several States
articles.summary: Several states have approved ballot measures restricting data center construction, potentially slowing growth in these facilities.
articles.content: Voters across several states have approved ballot measures that restrict data center construction, potentially slowing down the growth of these facilities. According to an analysis by Redbud Consulting, 37 such measures were passed as of Wednesday afternoon in California, Illinois, Maine, Ohio, New York, and other states. The election has also seen a number of candidates who campaigned on stricter regulation of data centers win their seats or advance to the next round. This could lead to increased scrutiny and new regulations for companies building these facilities. The growth of data centers has been fueled by demand from tech giants seeking to support emerging technologies like artificial intelligence. Franklin Templeton chief market strategist Stephen Dover predicts that the election results will have a significant impact on the construction of new data centers, citing concerns over costs and regulations. Meanwhile, technology analyst Dan Ives notes that the pushback against data center growth is "fueling the AI Revolution," as companies seek to reduce their environmental footprint and improve their public image. A temporary ban on data center construction could be implemented in Texas due to the recent gubernatorial election. Democrat Gina Hinojosa's victory over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott could stall the addition of 13 gigawatts of data-center power in the state. Hinojosa proposed a temporary ban on data center construction during her campaign, which would likely build upon Abbott's previous suspension of approvals for such projects. articles.title: Royal Gorge Route Railroad Offers Unique Perspective on Arkansas River Canyon
articles.summary: The 12-mile route follows the Arkansas River as it winds its way through a deep gorge carved out over millions of years.
articles.content: A train journey through Colorado's Royal Gorge offers passengers a unique perspective on one of the state's most breathtaking natural wonders. The 12-mile route follows the Arkansas River as it winds its way through a deep gorge carved out over millions of years. Royal Gorge Route Railroad engineer Adam Clawson is at the helm of "Black Betty, a powerful diesel-electric locomotive that has been running on this stretch for decades. With a background in railroading - his grandfather and great-grandfather both worked along this route - Clawson knows the history and geology of the area intimately. As the train rumbles through the gorge, Clawson provides a commentary on the geological forces that shaped this landscape over time. The Arkansas River has been wearing away the hard granite for millions of years, creating a V-shaped chasm that plunges as deep as 1,250 feet in places. The Royal Gorge is an awe-inspiring sight from any perspective - from above, where visitors can gaze down from the Royal Gorge Bridge, to below, where adventurous travelers can paddle the river's rapids on a whitewater raft. The Royal Gorge Route Railroad's open-air car offers an unobstructed view of the stunning canyon walls as it chugs along the historic route. This train line has been in operation for nearly 150 years, despite a rocky start when two competing railroad companies fought for control of the area in the late 1870s. The Denver & Rio Grande ultimately prevailed and built tracks through the narrow canyon, connecting to the mining hub of Leadville. The train's route is steeped in history, with its original construction dating back nearly a century and a half ago. Today, passengers can enjoy the same breathtaking views that pioneers and prospectors did during the height of the Old West era. Travelers can choose from three classes: Vista Dome, Deluxe Class, and Coach Class. The Vista Dome cars boast glass-enclosed domes offering panoramic views of the gorge, while Deluxe Class features vintage dining cars with cushioned booth-style seating and a bar. The train's route takes passengers on a scenic journey through the Royal Gorge, one of Colorado's most breathtaking natural wonders. On select dates, travelers can enjoy fine dining in First Class, with elevated menus and wine pairings available for both lunch and dinner. Regardless of their seating arrangement, all ticket holders have access to the open-air car, which offers standing-room only views of the surrounding landscape. This allows passengers to soak up the sights and sounds of the gorge without being confined to a specific seat. As the train navigates the twists and turns of the track, the scenery unfolds before the eyes of its passengers. With an experienced engineer at the controls, travelers can simply sit back and enjoy the ride, taking in the stunning vistas that surround them. As we continue our journey on this historic train, the scenery outside becomes even more breathtaking. The train chugs over the famous Hanging Bridge," a remarkable feat of engineering that has stood the test of time since its completion in 1879. The bridge's design was a major challenge due to the narrow chasm it spans, which is only about 30 feet wide at this point. To overcome this obstacle, an innovative solution was devised: a long suspension bridge supported by A-shaped structures anchored to the canyon wall. This clever engineering allows the train to pass through with ease. As we approach the western terminus of our journey, the town of Parkdale comes into view. The train's horn blares out in response to a group of kayakers standing on the bank, who wave and smile in greeting - no mooning today! The train slows down as it approaches its final stop, and passengers disembark onto the tracks. The imposing presence of the train is striking when viewed up close, especially considering Clawson's description of its personality. Standing in front of this massive machine, it's easy to imagine its independent spirit and self-assured nature. As we journey back to Cañon City, the train's engine hums smoothly in reverse gear, retracing the original route taken earlier. The rhythmic drone of the wheels on the tracks creates a soothing melody that helps me unwind. Outside, the rugged walls of the gorge continue to alternate between light and shadow, while the river sparkles in the sunlight above it. A turkey vulture soars effortlessly high overhead, its wings arched in a gentle V as it glides without flapping. articles.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sparked controversy by claiming there are "serious suspicions that foreign countries have spent large sums of money to influence the outcome of Israel's recent parliamentary elections. The prime minister's comments come as tensions rise between his government and Arab-Israeli politicians, who are seen as key players in determining the country's future leadership. The accusations have been met with resistance from the Joint List, a coalition of three Arab-Israeli parties that includes Ayman Odeh, one of its lawmakers. The list has denounced Netanyahu's claims as political persecution" and warned that such allegations aim to delegitimize the votes cast by Arab citizens in the October 27 election. The controversy surrounding foreign interference in Israel's elections comes as the country is set for a new round of coalition-building. With several key parties still undecided on their allegiances, Netanyahu's far-right allies are seeking to capitalize on his claims of foreign meddling to sway public opinion and secure their positions. The Joint List has stated that it will not allow its supporters' votes to be discredited by such allegations, and is vowing to continue working towards a united front with other opposition parties. The investigation into alleged foreign interference in Israel's recent elections has taken a new turn, with outgoing lawmaker Odeh set to be questioned by Shin Bet officials. Odeh, a veteran of Israeli politics and former leader of the left-wing party Hadash, is accused of receiving hundreds of thousands of shekels from an unspecified foreign entity. The allegations have been pushed by Netanyahu's Likud party, which claims they raise serious concerns about election fairness. The Attorney General has denied Shin Bet's request to interrogate other Arab party leaders without concrete evidence, sparking anger among Netanyahu's allies who have long had a tense relationship with the Attorney General. Meanwhile, Netanyahu is pointing to recent arrests of individuals found with cash on election day as evidence of localized incidents rather than widespread foreign interference. Netanyahu has leveled further accusations against his opponents, claiming they have accepted money from Qatar in an attempt to sway the election outcome. The premier's assertion appears to be part of a broader narrative aimed at undermining confidence in the electoral process. articles.content: Elon Musk's massive investment in Republican midterm victories has fallen short of its expected outcome. The tech mogul donated at least $474 million to Republican candidates ahead of the 2026 elections, nearly doubling his previous contribution to the party. A significant portion of this sum went towards election efforts in Texas alone, with around $200 million allocated for various campaigns. This investment was largely focused on supporting Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton and Governor Greg Abbott, both of whom suffered defeats at the hands of their Democratic opponents. The outcome has had an immediate impact on Musk's business interests in the state. Shares of SpaceX and Tesla, both headquartered in Texas, experienced a decline following the news of the election results. This development may signal a loss of confidence among investors in the region. Musk's significant donation to Republican causes was part of a larger trend. The billionaire joined other notable donors such as Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz of a16z, who contributed $116.4 million, and Greg Brockman and his wife Anna, co-founders of OpenAI, who donated $50 million. The outcome has left many questioning the effectiveness of large-scale campaign donations in achieving their intended goals. According to Logan Phillips, founder of the election forecasting site Race to the White House, this election may mark a significant defeat for big money in politics in American history. While Elon Musk's $474 million loss may seem like a significant setback, it remains unclear whether this will impact his influence on key Republicans or if he is laying the groundwork for future elections. Campaign finance experts argue that Musk's investments in the election were not solely focused on securing specific outcomes, but rather aimed at shaping the broader conversation around issues such as climate change and economic reform. According to Virginia Commonwealth University political science professor Alex Keena, "money is affecting what we're talking about" when it comes to campaign financing. This means that donations often dictate which topics are prioritized by parties, rather than determining election outcomes themselves. Musk's significant investments in the Republican party suggest a level of commitment to President Donald Trump, who could potentially prove to be an ally as Musk navigates complex business dealings, including his pursuit of a SpaceX-Tesla merger. The scrutiny surrounding this merger from Democrats may create a situation where Musk and Trump find common ground, further solidifying Musk's influence within the Republican party. This scrutiny could potentially set the agenda for what issues are discussed in 2028, as Keena noted that "it's not just about who wins. It's about setting the agenda and what types of issues we talk about." The influence of money in politics is significant, and Musk's involvement has been substantial. However, while Trump has threatened to veto legislation passed by a Democratic majority, Democrats have a powerful tool at their disposal: subpoena powers. These do not require the president's signature, allowing officials to investigate Musk's public companies and his role in the federal government without obstruction. Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) was criticized for its failure to achieve one of its primary goals - reducing the federal deficit. Furthermore, DOGE gained unauthorized access to sensitive data, raising serious concerns about the handling of classified information. As part of this investigation, Democrats plan to scrutinize Musk's involvement with DOGE and his role in the private sector. Sara Guerrero, a spokesperson for Rep. Robert Garcia, stated that "we definitely have a lot of questions about Elon Musk's role in DOGE" and intend to look into it further. The extent of Musk's influence extends beyond his public companies, as his connections to government officials have led to significant financial gains for his private sector ventures. A Washington Post analysis found that two dozen former DOGE staffers leveraged their government connections to secure funding, with startups backed by these individuals raising over $500 million in venture capital and funding. The high-profile endorsement of certain Republican candidates by Elon Musk may have had unintended consequences on his own influence and reputation. Musk's decision to inject himself into the White House and dominate campaign donation landscapes has been seen as a risk that could backfire, according to some analysts. The public display of power may have turned off potential voters and diminished his impact on future elections. This development could be a significant blow to Musk's ability to shape the 2028 elections. Musk's financial backing is no longer viewed as an asset but rather a liability, affecting both those who receive it and himself.
